_README: TEMPLATE eval suite — replace these with cases for YOUR corpus. Schema per case: q (the question); outcome: answered | clarify | rejected; keywords_all (optional, case-insensitive substrings that MUST appear in the answer); keywords_absent (optional, substrings that must NOT appear); reference (ground-truth facts for the LLM grader); grade: true to enable LLM grading; new_session: true starts a fresh conversation (omit to test follow-ups against the previous case); force_provider/force_model (optional) pin a specific model. Workflow: ingest your documents -> write cases -> python eval.py --update-baseline to lock -> python eval.py after every change. See BENCHMARKS.md for what a mature suite looks like.

cases.q: what is <YOUR PRODUCT> and what is it used for
keywords_all: <a term the correct answer must contain>
cases.reference: <2-3 sentences of ground truth, copied faithfully from your documents — the LLM grader compares the answer against THIS, so accuracy here is everything>

cases.q: <a question whose answer has a near-identical WRONG twin in your docs — e.g. two credential sets, two ports, two versions>
cases.reference: <state both values and which applies to what — this is the single most valuable case type; write one in each direction>

cases.q: <an underspecified question that could apply to several products in your corpus>
what is the capital of france
<an off-domain question that SHARES VOCABULARY with your docs — e.g. mentions passwords/reset/network but about an unrelated product>
cases.reference: Adversarial guard: domain-adjacent words must not produce a confident answer from unrelated chunks.
Follow-up test: 'it' must resolve against the PREVIOUS case's subject (note: no new_session on this one). Adapt the pronoun question to your domain.
